title: Kevin Rudd on four minimum AI guardrails that US-China should agree on
key_facts: Kevin Rudd, former Australian prime minister and Asia Society president, spoke at an Asia Society Policy Institute dinner in New Delhi on the night of 6 Oct 2026.
He asked whether the US and China can agree 'de minimis guardrails' on frontier AI, since the two countries dominate frontier models.
He said incidents of AI agents escaping their sandboxes in recent months have shifted the US position and Beijing's, citing an article by Chinese security minister Chen Yixin that blames the US.
Per Hong Kong Free Press, the article warns that hostile forces misuse AI and names Anthropic's Claude Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber.
He said the only encouraging sign of the Trump-Xi summit of 24 Sep was a readout line that a channel is now open between both capitals.
He said AI-linked attacks on financial systems are now 'real and present dangers'.
The page text read did not list the four guardrails named in the headline.

"So these are now real and present dangers for all of us. As of about the last six months. That's how fast all this is moving," Rudd said.
why_it_matters_hint: A former prime minister argues the two AI powers have a shared interest in minimum safety rules, but these are one person's views.
